items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Bina Chaudhari and Parth Choudhary, Simply Smart Childcare
notes:
B. Chaudhari and P. Choudhary provided a presentation on the need for affordable childcare spaces. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. B. Chaudhary expressed concerns that their organization Simply Smart Childcare has been excluded from the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) funding.

In response to the Committee, B. Cardow, Director of Children's Services, clarified that the Region is required to maintain 90% non-profit to 10% for-profit childcare spaces.

The Committee directed staff to provide a report on CWELCC funding as it relates to childcare spaces statistics, the number of childcare spots that have been allocated and when they will be filled, the number of spots currently filled and in operation, and information on the capital budget and the operating budget and if there is any unused funding. The report should also provide information related to any long-term implication, if any, of changing the current processes.

items.title: Theo Yu, Waterloo
notes: T. Yu requested that the Committee consider a by-law to permit public camping. They explained that there is a lack of shelter spaces in the Region of Waterloo and that all individuals have a right to shelter.

items.title: Sky Dasey
notes: S. Dasey expressed concern that there is a lack of access to shelter spaces and affordable housing. She requested that the Committee focus on investment over enforcement.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-PSV-25-006, Paramedic Services Master Plan 2026-2035
notes:
John Riches, Director and Chief of Paramedic Services, introduced the presentation. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. He highlighted the 2025 key performance indicators which demonstrate significant improvement, specifically with the reduction of both offload delays and Code Zero events. 

Hannah Mayers-Frenett, ORH Senior Consultant, provided a presentation on the Paramedic Services Master Plan for 2026-2035. She discussed projected scenarios based on demand. She identified the recommended facility configuration, and she set out a phased approach to best use the frontline resources and facilities either by prioritizing performance or utilization. She further identified several recommendations including the development of a digital strategy
and Service Level Agreements across support services. Based on the Region's projected growth in the next ten years they identified that there will need to be an increase to resources including full-time staff and facility reconfiguration and enhancements.

J. Riches confirmed that the staff recommendation to approve the proposed Paramedic Services Master Plan is subject to the annual budget approval process. 

Responding to the Committee, J. Riches confirmed that the Region is working on creating strategies that would support staff development, however, the training cost to become an Advanced Care Paramedic is significant. J. Riches further confirmed that community-paramedicine program expansion would assist in decreasing emergency calls and care delays. Community paramedicine is 100% funded by the province and they announced that the funding will become permanent funding instead of annualized grant funding on April 1, 2026. Staff are waiting to hear what the funding level will be set at. The Williamsburg site in Kitchener was previously identified in the existing master plan as an optimal site based its location and will assist in response times for the entire Region as resources from other area municipalities will not need to be redirected to that area.

Responding to comments from Committee, J. Riches explained that the 70% decrease in offload delays was due to the prioritization of this issue by staff and the ongoing effort to meet with hospital leadership every two weeks to address these issues. He explained that the new dispatching system will provide paramedics with information that allows for better distribution of resources

In response to the Committee, H. Mayer-Frenett clarifed that there is a balance between having resources available while ensuring that resources and being optimally utilized. She noted that if the urban areas are better served will ultimately benefit the rural areas as paramedic services share resources. H. Mayer-Frenett further clarified that as the plan for the new hospital is still being solidified the paramedic services master plan does not fully address its integration, but as more information is released the paramedic services plan will be adjusted accordingly.

Responding to questions of the Committee related to paramedic staff retention, J. Riches explained that paramedics can suffer from burnout caused by the physical and mental stresses of the job. He noted that having additional staff on rotation is critical as paramedics require relief for sick time, vacation time, and training time. Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner of Public Health & Paramedic Services and Medical Officer of Health, further noted that burnout and the increase of WSIB claims is a provincially wide issue.

Responding to the Committee, J. Riches agreed that alternative destinations are important to provide paramedics the opportunity to manage each emergency call on an individual basis that would better address public needs and help to reduce the strain on hospital emergency rooms. Dr. H. Wang confirmed staff will continue to look for opportunities for advocacy for funding supports. J. Riches further confirmed that all paramedic services must adhere to applicable legislation which may limit innovation to address certain needs such as supporting rural areas. He highlighted that the Region has a mixed community of both rural and urban municipalities.

The Committee expressed concerns about ensuring equitable service access for all area municipalities including rural areas and the City of Cambridge.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-25-008, COCHI-OPHI Year 7, 8 and 9 Investment Plan and Expansion Target Forecast Report
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with regard to Year 7 (2025/26) of the Canada-Ontario Community Housing Initiative (COCHI), the Ontario Priorities Housing Initiative (OPHI), and the Expansion Target Forecast Report and Year 8 (2026/27) and Year 9 (2027/28) as outlined in report CSD-HOU-25-008 dated September 9, 2025: Approve the recommended Year 7 Investment Plan and Expansion Target Forecast Report for submission to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing; Authorize the Commissioner, Community Services Department, to execute such agreements and documentation in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as may be required to process the advance of funding for these programs; Authorize the Commissioner, Community Service Department, with delegated authority to approve the Year 8 and 9 Investment Plan and Expansion Target Forecast Report as funding is confirmed for submission to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing; Authorize Director, Housing Services, to execute and deliver all other documentation required by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing and the Region of Waterloo to allocate funding from COCHI and OPHI.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with regard to Year 7 (2025/26) of the Canada-Ontario Community Housing Initiative (COCHI), the Ontario Priorities Housing Initiative (OPHI), and the Expansion Target Forecast Report and Year 8 (2026/27) and Year 9 (2027/28) as outlined in report CSD-HOU-25-008 dated September 9, 2025:

  1. Approve the recommended Year 7 Investment Plan and Expansion Target Forecast Report for submission to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing;
  2. Authorize the Commissioner, Community Services Department, to execute such agreements and documentation in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as may be required to process the advance of funding for these programs;
  3. Authorize the Commissioner, Community Service Department, with delegated authority to approve the Year 8 and 9 Investment Plan and Expansion Target Forecast Report as funding is confirmed for submission to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing;
  4. Authorize Director, Housing Services, to execute and deliver all other documentation required by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing and the Region of Waterloo to allocate funding from COCHI and OPHI.

motions.item_title: PHP-PSV-25-004, Paramedic Services Response Time Performance Plan 2026
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Response Time Performance Plan (RTPP) for 2026, outlined below, in accordance with the Ambulance Act, O. Reg. 267/08, amending O. Reg. 257/00, under Part VII, Response Time Performance Plans, Sections 22-24, as outlined in PHP-PSV-25-004, dated September 9, 2025. Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) – 6 minutes or less 70% of the time. (Note: Ministry of Health target is 50%.) CTAS 1 – 8 minutes or less 70% of the time. CTAS 2 – 10 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 3 – 15 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 4 – 20 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 5 – 25 minutes or less 80% of the time.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Response Time Performance Plan (RTPP) for 2026, outlined below, in accordance with the Ambulance Act, O. Reg. 267/08, amending O.
